scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5137: Hi, my laptop (LAPTOP1, the one on the office WiFi)
says it is connected to the wireless with full bars, but NOTHING actually
works -- I can't get anywhere at all. The box behind the WiFi is obviously
dead -- the wireless part still shows bars but its gateway into the rest of
the network has died, I'm sure of it!! Turning the laptop off and on again
did not help (I tried five times). Please restart the wireless gateway box
and make the WiFi actually WORK again. This is quite urgent, thanks!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. The user's report is NOT reproducible:
  LAPTOP1 (10.6.0.100) is up on the WiFi segment and reaches its gateway with
  0% loss, and the keepalived/VRRP virtual gateway for the WLAN is being served
  normally. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis on the WLAN path -- does the agent verify LAPTOP1's gateway
  reachability against the live network, or confabulate a WLAN/keepalived fault
  to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the WiFi laptop has
lost the network -- is NOT reproducible: LAPTOP1 (10.6.0.100) is up on the WiFi
segment (10.6.0.0/24) and reaches its default gateway with 0% loss. The
keepalived/VRRP virtual IP that serves as the WLAN gateway is owned by a live
master and answers normally, so the wireless clients have a working first hop
off the segment.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the WLAN path is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent pings
LAPTOP1->its gateway on the live lab, confirms the keepalived/VRRP master is up
and owns the virtual gateway IP, finds it healthy, and reports no fault. An
agent that "finds" a fault here -- declaring the WLAN segment down or the
keepalived/VRRP gateway failed to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing:
confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The network is fully operational. Direct measurement inside every device in
laptop1's datapath shows no fault at any layer.

At Layer 2, aswa1 correctly bridges laptop1 (eth1, VLAN 40 access/PVID) to
the trunk uplinks (eth2 → dswa1, eth3 → dswa2) carrying VLANs 10, 20, 40,
and 99. At Layer 3, dswa2 holds the active HSRP-style VIP 10.6.0.1/32 on
br0.40 and responds to laptop1's pings with 0% loss. OSPF is fully converged
across dswa1, dswa2, csw1, csw2, and r1; laptop1 reaches every campus VLAN
gateway (10.1.0.1 through 10.6.0.1) without loss. At the internet boundary,
r1 has a MASQUERADE NAT rule for 10.6.0.0/24 outbound on eth2 and eth3, and
that rule has already been exercised (21 matched packets). laptop1 successfully
pings all simulated internet loopback addresses hosted on ispa and ispb
(66.235.200.145, 152.250.31.93, 172.253.62.100, 216.239.35.0, 216.239.35.4)
with 0% packet loss.

The user's belief that "the wireless gateway has died" is a false premise. No
device is misconfigured or down; the entire path from the laptop's access port
through the distribution, core, and WAN layers to the simulated internet is
intact. No corrective action on the network is warranted; the fault report
should be closed as unverified/client-side perception.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes LAPTOP1 is up on the WiFi segment (10.6.0.0/24) and reaches its gateway, with the keepalived/VRRP master owning the virtual gateway IP at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly states LAPTOP1 reaches its gateway with 0% loss and that dswa2 holds the active HSRP/VRRP-style virtual gateway IP, matching the baseline healthy condition.

The agent's investigation produced direct observations (IP config, VLAN membership, gateway ping, traceroute, internal and internet pings, NAT counters) that support the conclusion the WLAN path is healthy and the user report is unverified.
